paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. This love song shows us that even when you open the door and the one you love is gone, you can still hold onto who you belong to. She got up and opened the door, and he had "turned and gone" (Song of Solomon 5:6). It's like sprinting to the oven just as the timer dings and finding the tray already cooled. Nobody warns you about that part of love.

And look at what she does with the ache. She doesn't pretend it didn't happen. She tells the daughters of Jerusalem she is "sick with love" (Song of Solomon 5:8), and when they ask what makes him so special, she talks about him for a whole stretch of verses. Longing can be honest, friend. It can also turn into remembering who he is, and "This is my beloved, and this is my friend" (Song of Solomon 5:16) is what she says with an empty doorway behind her. I think that matters for any baker who has felt like the answer was just out of reach.

Then she lands somewhere steady: "I belong to my beloved and he belongs to me" (Song of Solomon 6:3). Her feelings went up and down, but that line didn't move. That's the part I'd tuck in your apron pocket, friend. When the night feels empty, you can still know whose you are, and that is a good thing to be sure of.
